Kubota and Kilter expand AX-1 robot distribution across Europe

 09-10 | Autonomous vehicles | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

The autonomous Kilter AX-1 uses cameras and AI to detect individual weeds and applies small droplets of herbicide directly onto the target. Kilter says 66 AX-1 robots are currently in operation. Photo: Peter Roek

Kubota and Norwegian robotics company Kilter have signed a European framework agreement to expand sales and support for the AX-1 autonomous spot-spraying robot. Already commercially available in Germany and the Netherlands, the robot is now being considered for markets including France and the UK.

The agreement builds on an existing partnership between the two companies in Germany and the Netherlands. Kubota will use its European dealer, parts and service network to support a step-by-step expansion of the Kilter AX-1 into additional European markets. Kilter spare parts are already stocked at Kubota’s European Parts Centre in Thionville, France. Participating dealers can order AX-1 parts through the same system used for Kubota equipment.

Targeting individual weeds

The AX-1 is an autonomous field robot developed primarily for high-value crops such as vegetables and herbs. Cameras and AI-based machine vision identify individual weeds, after which Kilter’s Single Drop Technology applies small droplets of herbicide directly onto the target. Kilter claims the approach can reduce herbicide use by up to 95% compared with conventional applications, depending on conditions and application. The company says 66 AX-1 robots are currently in operation and together have avoided the use of more than one million litres of herbicide.

France and UK considered next

The European framework agreement was signed on 22 July by Kilter managing director Kristoffer Magnor and Kubota Holdings Europe president Shinichi Yamada. The companies are currently exploring further expansion into France and the UK. For Kilter, the agreement provides access to a larger established dealer and service infrastructure. Kubota, meanwhile, is adding an autonomous precision weeding system to its European smart farming portfolio.

No timetable was given for introduction into the additional European markets.

translationZh:
久保田与挪威机器人公司Kilter签署了一项欧洲框架协议，以扩大AX-1自主点喷除草机器人的销售和支持。该机器人已在德国和荷兰实现商业化，目前正考虑进入法国和英国等市场。

该协议建立在两家公司于德国和荷兰现有合作基础之上。久保田将利用其欧洲经销商、零部件和服务网络，支持Kilter AX-1逐步扩展至更多欧洲市场。Kilter备件已存放在久保田位于法国蒂永维尔的欧洲零部件中心。参与经销商可通过与久保田设备相同的系统订购AX-1零件。

**精准靶向单株杂草**

AX-1是一款自主田间机器人，主要面向蔬菜和香草等高价值作物开发。摄像头和基于AI的机器视觉可识别单株杂草，随后Kilter的Single Drop技术将少量除草剂直接施用于目标。Kilter声称，根据条件和应用情况，该方法相比传统施药可减少高达95%的除草剂用量。该公司表示，目前有66台AX-1机器人正在运行，累计避免了超过100万升除草剂的使用。

**法国和英国或为下一步**

该欧洲框架协议于7月22日由Kilter总经理Kristoffer Magnor和久保田欧洲控股总裁Shinichi Yamada签署。两家公司目前正在探索进一步扩展至法国和英国。对Kilter而言，该协议提供了进入更大型成熟经销商和服务基础设施的渠道。与此同时，久保田正在为其欧洲智慧农业产品组合增添一套自主精准除草系统。

尚未公布进入更多欧洲市场的时间表。
